# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`

## Goal

**User story:** As a producer, I want the before/after bot-batch evidence and the scaling documentation in one place, so the change can be reviewed on evidence and future tuning has a written baseline.

Implements "Desired change" step 6 and the parent ACs "Automated balance evidence" and "Documentation" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

- Run a same-seed **baseline batch** (100 games, competent policy) with the level curves disabled (pre-change behaviour) and a **post-change batch**, using the extended per-level harness mode. Record both in the parent work item and in `docs/BALANCING.md`.
- Record per-level `powerUpsCollected`, `enemiesKilledByArchetype`, `avoidableHits`, `survivalSeconds` and `levelReached`; show mid/late-level power-up supply per enemy is below baseline and that the reached-level/completion metric does not regress and nothing crashes.
- If the evidence shows the endpoints are wrong, adjust the tuning data within the agreed curve shape (linear count ramp, monotonic non-increasing drop chance) and re-run; document the final values and the reason.
- Update `docs/BALANCING.md` (scaling table + evidence + how to reproduce), the GDD power-up and level sections, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` if the wave-build seam description changed, plus README/related docs references.
- Record the documented divergence for formation gyms (no campaign-level context) in the parent work item and alongside the code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Baseline and post-change batches are recorded with the per-level metrics listed above, the exact command and commit hashes, and the same seed set.
- Evidence shows lower per-kill power-up supply at mid/late levels than baseline and no fall in the reached-level/completion metric; no crash in either batch.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the curves (table for levels 1–10), the rationale and how to reproduce the evidence.
- GDD power-up/level sections and any other affected docs/README references are updated.
- Docs assertions (`src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`, `evaluationDocs.test.ts`) pass.
- No tuning change is made outside the agreed curve shape without recording it as a new work item.

- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Automated balance evidence** — The deterministic evaluation harness can measure the change (extend the arena/batch so a run can exercise the real campaign waves and the real per-kill drop rule, at least for L1/L5/L10). Record a same-seed **baseline batch (100 games, competent policy)** against HEAD and a **post-change batch** in the work item or `docs/BALANCING.md`, including per-level `powerUpsCollected`, `enemiesKilledByArchetype`, `avoidableHits`, `survivalSeconds` and `levelReached`. The evidence must show the mid/late-level power-up supply per enemy is below baseline and that the campaign remains playable (no crash, no fall in the batch's reached-level/completion metric).
- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Documentation** — `docs/BALANCING.md` (scaling table + evidence), the GDD power-up/level sections and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (if the wave-build seam changes) are updated with the new behaviour and tuning rationale; code comments document the curves.
- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Key Files

- `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md`
- `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`, `src/ai/eval/evaluationDocs.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: the campaign count-application, drop-chance, level-gym parity and harness-extension features.

data.description:
## Problem

The integration test `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde (AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6) > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` failed once on the AI_Hell full suite under heavy machine load (multiple concurrent full suites from other repos), then **passed on a fresh full-suite re-run** (298 files / 6582 tests passed) minutes later with the same code. It is flaky, not a regression.

Failure (from `implement.py finish` for AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H, docs-only change):

```
FAIL |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6168:26
    6166|     scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
    6167|     scene.tick(0.001);
    6168|     expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
```

The same run also printed repeated `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` on stderr (unrelated noise; no test failed on it).

## Why it is flaky

The test spawns a bullet exactly at the victim and advances the scene by a single **1 ms** tick, then asserts the kill. Under load, the physics/collision step for that tick may not process the new projectile before the assertion, so `victim.alive` is still true. It passes when the machine is less loaded.

## Suggested fix

Make the kill assertion independent of one tick's scheduling: advance a realistic frame (e.g. `scene.tick(0.05)`) or tick until the victim is dead with a small bounded loop and assert the outcome, keeping the wave-accounting assertion (`wm.enemiesAlive === total - 1`) afterwards. Do not weaken the assertion - the test must still prove the kill is counted exactly once.

## Acceptance criteria

- The test no longer fails under load (run the full suite while other suites are active, or add a deterministic tick/loop that does not depend on a 1 ms step).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` still asserts the grunt dies and wave accounting decreases by exactly one.
- Full suite passes (test skill gate).

## Evidence / references

- Discovered during AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H (docs-only change; cannot affect PlayScene kill behaviour).
- Failure observed 2026-10-24 ~13:16 UTC; green full-suite rerun at ~13:07 UTC (298 files / 6582 tests) with the identical worktree tree.
- `discovered-from:AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H`.
data.title: Fix flaky PlayScene Robotron horde kill test under load
